external_entities.name: member
external_entities.source_excerpt: Members collect points when they shop

external_entities.name: browser
external_entities.description: A member's browser used to sign in and approve consent.
external_entities.source_excerpt: signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser

external_entities.name: partner app
external_entities.description: A web application run by another company on its own server.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers

processes.name: mobile app
processes.description: The mobile application used by members to sign in, obtain tokens, call the rewards API, and disconnect partner apps.
processes.notes: PKCE challenge support is not recorded. The app keeps a refresh token on the phone.

processes.name: authorization server
processes.description: The authorization server handling member sign-in, authorization codes, consent, refresh tokens, and access tokens.
processes.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts
processes.notes: The server signs tokens for the support console with the same key used for other tokens.

processes.name: rewards API
processes.description: The API called by mobile and partner applications to access rewards and points operations.
processes.source_excerpt: then calls the rewards API with the access token it gets back
processes.notes: The API does not check which client or audience a token was issued for.

processes.name: support console
processes.description: A web application that closes a member's account.
processes.source_excerpt: The support console is a web app that closes a member's account.
processes.notes: It is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.

data_stores.name: identity database
data_stores.description: Database containing member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database
data_stores.notes: Refresh tokens remain in this database when an account is closed.

data_stores.name: points ledger
data_stores.description: Ledger containing every member's balance and every points transaction.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the points ledger, which holds every member's balance and every points transaction
data_stores.notes: The ledger records which client made each change, but not which member approved it.

data_stores.name: API log store
data_stores.description: Store receiving every request received by the rewards API, including headers.
data_stores.source_excerpt: writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store

data_flows.name: use mobile app
data_flows.description: A member uses the mobile app.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members use our mobile app.
data_flows.notes: unknown
data_flows.data_description: Member interactions with the mobile application

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: The mobile app signs the member in through the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow
data_flows.notes: The source does not state whether the app sends a PKCE challenge.

data_flows.name: call API
data_flows.description: The mobile app calls the rewards API using an access token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: then calls the rewards API with the access token it gets back
data_flows.notes: Access tokens are plain bearer tokens and live for one hour.

data_flows.name: disconnect app
data_flows.description: The mobile app requests disconnection of a partner app from the settings screen.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members can disconnect a partner app from the settings screen of the mobile app
data_flows.notes: The source states that the partner app's refresh token is deleted from the identity database.

data_flows.name: request tokens
data_flows.description: A partner app sends token requests to the authorization server using its client secret.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The partner app sends that secret in the body of its token requests.
data_flows.notes: The client secret is sent in the request body.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: The member's browser submits sign-in and consent interactions to the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A member who connects a partner app signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser
data_flows.notes: The authorization-server sign-in is kept in a cookie for thirty days; no idle timeout was decided.
data_flows.data_description: Member sign-in, consent, and session-cookie data

data_flows.name: return code
data_flows.description: The browser returns an authorization code to the partner app's redirect URI.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The browser then returns to the partner app's redirect URI with an authorization code.
data_flows.notes: The authorization code stays valid for ten minutes.

data_flows.name: show points
data_flows.description: A partner app calls the rewards API to show a member's points.
data_flows.source_excerpt: a meal-planning service that shows a member's points
data_flows.notes: unknown

data_flows.name: store identity data
data_flows.description: The authorization server stores and retrieves identity and authorization data in the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database
data_flows.notes: This includes authorization codes, refresh tokens, consents, and deletion of a disconnected partner app's refresh token.
data_flows.data_description: Accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents

data_flows.name: update ledger
data_flows.description: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger
data_flows.notes: unknown

data_flows.name: write requests
data_flows.description: The rewards API writes received requests and headers to the API log store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store
data_flows.notes: unknown

data_flows.name: obtain token
data_flows.description: The support console takes access tokens from the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It takes access tokens from the same authorization server
data_flows.notes: The source does not specify how the support console obtains the tokens.

data_flows.name: close account
data_flows.description: The support console marks a member's account closed in the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Closing an account marks it closed in the identity database.
data_flows.notes: The member's refresh tokens remain in the same database.

trust_boundaries.name: own cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: The organisation's own cloud account hosting the system components and stores described in the system.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Everything below runs in our own cloud account

trust_boundaries.name: member phones
trust_boundaries.description: The members' phones, outside the organisation's cloud account.

trust_boundaries.name: partner servers
trust_boundaries.description: Servers run by other companies hosting partner applications.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: other companies run on their own servers

assumptions.assumption: The mobile app runs on the members' phones.
assumptions.basis: The description distinguishes the members' phones from the organisation's own cloud account and says members use the mobile app.

assumptions.assumption: The partner app is hosted in the partner servers boundary.
assumptions.basis: The description says partner apps are run by other companies on their own servers.

assumptions.assumption: The rewards API is internet-facing.
assumptions.basis: The rewards API is accessed by partner servers and is served on the same public hostname as the support console.

assumptions.assumption: The support console is internet-facing.
assumptions.basis: The description says the support console is served on a public hostname.

assumptions.assumption: The identity database contains confidential data.
assumptions.basis: It contains member email addresses, password hashes, refresh tokens, authorization codes, and consents.

assumptions.assumption: The points ledger contains confidential data.
assumptions.basis: It contains every member's balance and every points transaction.

assumptions.assumption: The API log store contains confidential data.
assumptions.basis: It stores every API request and its headers, which can include bearer access tokens.

assumptions.assumption: The member carries personal data.
assumptions.basis: A member is the person associated with the loyalty account and points activity.

assumptions.assumption: The mobile app handles credentials, personal data, and financial data.
assumptions.basis: It handles refresh tokens, member sign-in, access tokens, and rewards requests.

assumptions.assumption: The authorization server handles credentials, personal data, and secrets.
assumptions.basis: It handles password hashes, tokens, member accounts, authorization codes, consents, and token signing.

assumptions.assumption: The rewards API handles credentials, personal data, financial data, and operating ledger data.
assumptions.basis: It uses access tokens and reads and writes the points ledger.

assumptions.assumption: The support console handles credentials, personal data, and financial data.
assumptions.basis: It uses access tokens and closes member accounts containing loyalty information.

assumptions.assumption: The identity flow carries credentials and personal data.
assumptions.basis: The flow carries the identity and authorization data stored by the authorization server.

assumptions.assumption: The support-console account-closing flow carries credentials and personal data.
assumptions.basis: It uses an access token and changes a member account.
